answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to earn trust slowly through bonded work history: a new agent must lock a deposit and complete small verifiable tasks over time before handling larger trades, like a sparrow building a nest twig by twig rather than appearing fully formed. To forge many fake identities, an attacker must fund many deposits and wait through many slow histories, while a glacier of public audit records makes cloned identities visible and slashable, so faking costs more than one extra vote or deal gains.
